title_prefix: Reconciliation sets never shed the entri
mechanism: Core has no counterpart at d3056bc, exactly as the finding states: refs/bitcoin/src/node/txreconciliation.cpp is 170 lines and its whole public surface is PreRegisterPeer, RegisterPeer, ForgetPeer and IsPeerRegistered (refs/bitcoin/src/node/txreconciliation.h:52-140), with in-tree TODOs saying the state fields are not used yet; the header's protocol sketch (:26-46) describes adding transactions to a set and reconciling, but no set, sketch or round exists in the code. So this is judged against BIP-330 and against the protocol's own invariant, not against Core, and our file says so in its header comment (src/networking/txreconciliation-set.lisp:5-12). The invariant: after a SUCCESSFUL round both sides know every transaction in the snapshot -- the ones in the symmetric difference because they were requested or announced, the ones that cancelled because both sides already held them -- so no entry from that snapshot can ever appear in a future difference with this peer. Our code removes only the difference. recon-finish-round (src/networking/txreconciliation-set.lisp:244-261) remhashes the ids in recon-round-ours-to-announce, i.e. the decoded ids we hold; %handle-reconcildiff (src/networking/protocol.lisp:2975-2996) remhashes only the ids the initiator asked for. The ids that cancelled in the sketch are in neither list and stay for the life of the connection. recon-set-add (:50-57) has no cap, and recon-set-remove (:58-60) has NO caller anywhere in src/, so there is no eviction when a transaction leaves the mempool either.
consequence: Two costs, and the second is the larger. Memory: one 32-bit key plus a 32-byte wtxid plus hash-table overhead per transaction we ever relayed to that peer and it already had, accumulating monotonically for the life of the connection with no cap and no mempool-driven eviction. Bandwidth and CPU: the retained entries are included in every subsequent snapshot, so recon-estimate-capacity (= |local-remote| + q*min(local,remote) + c, :91-104) sizes every future sketch against the accumulated dead weight instead of the real difference -- measured growing from 28 to 253 over ten rounds while the true difference stayed at 2 -- which destroys the bandwidth saving Erlay exists to deliver and makes decoding progressively more expensive. Reachability keeps it S3: -txreconciliation is default-off (src/config-options.lisp:89) and gates %recon-hold-p through the sendtxrcncl handshake (src/networking/protocol.lisp:3008-3026), and no Core peer at d3056bc implements any message past sendtxrcncl, so both ends must be our own nodes run with the flag. Not a peer-drivable lever, but genuinely unbounded once the flag is on at both ends.
evidence: Probe ga11-txrelay-recon-set (scripts/dev.sh load + eval), warm image bitcoin-lisp-sbcl:2.6.5-4, driving the initiator role directly (recon-start-round, a responder sketch built over the peer's ids with the same salt pair, recon-round-decode, recon-finish-round). (1) Control, the peer holds nothing so every entry is in the difference: (:CAPACITY 21 :DECODED 20 :ASK 0 :ANNOUNCE 20 :SET-SIZE-BEFORE 20 :SET-SIZE-AFTER 0) -- removal works when the ids are in the difference. (2) The finding, 100 shared plus 5 ours-only: (:CAPACITY 31 :DECODED 5 :ASK 0 :ANNOUNCE 5 :SET-SIZE-BEFORE 105 :SET-SIZE-AFTER 100) -- the 5 differing ids leave, the 100 shared ids stay. (3) Ten consecutive successful rounds, 100 newly relayed shared transactions plus 2 unshared per round: (:SET-SIZE-AFTER-EACH-ROUND (100 200 300 400 500 600 700 800 900 1000) :SKETCH-CAPACITY-EACH-ROUND (28 53 78 103 128 153 178 203 228 253) :DECODED-DIFFERENCE-EACH-ROUND (2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2)) -- monotone set growth with the real difference constant, and the sketch capacity growing in lockstep. (4) Second positive control on the other removal path: recon-abandon-round on a 20-entry set gave (:ANNOUNCED-ON-ABANDON 20 :SET-SIZE-AFTER 0), so the flood fallback does clear and the retention above is specific to the success path. Side observation while building the probe: with two IDENTICAL sets the decode yields an empty list, which recon-round-decode (:170-183) reports as failure because it tests the list for truth, so a perfectly reconciled pair takes the extension-then-flood path; that is a separate defect and is noted here only because it is what relieves the accumulation in the fully-shared case. Ours: src/networking/txreconciliation-set.lisp:50-60, :91-104, :170-183, :244-261, :263-278; src/networking/protocol.lisp:2906-2908, :2975-2996, :3008-3026; src/config-options.lisp:89. Core at d3056bc: refs/bitcoin/src/node/txreconciliation.cpp (170 lines, handshake only), refs/bitcoin/src/node/txreconciliation.h:26-140.
fix_shape: Clear the snapshot at the end of a successful round on both sides, which is what the protocol's own invariant requires: after SUCCESS every id in the frozen snapshot is known to both peers, so recon-finish-round and %handle-reconcildiff should remove the whole snapshot rather than only the ids in the difference -- the differing ids are already handled (announced by us or requested from them) and the cancelling ids are by definition held by both. recon-abandon-round already does exactly this removal over recon-round-local-ids (:263-278) and is the shape to copy; the responder half needs the same treatment, which means %handle-reconcildiff must clear the snapshot's ids and not just the asked-for ones before it calls recon-set-clear-snapshot. Two follow-ons belong with it. Give recon-set-remove the callers it lacks so a transaction evicted or mined out of the mempool leaves every peer's reconciliation set, mirroring the mempool-removal hook the inv path already gets at flush time (protocol.lisp:3040-3044). And put a cap on recon-set-add sized against the peer's announcement budget, so a set can never grow past what one round could ever reconcile even if a round never completes. Because none of this has a Core oracle, each change wants a test that asserts the set size after a round rather than only the announcements it produced -- the current tests check the difference and would stay green through all of the above.
